NVDA.thesis: NVIDIA remains the essential infrastructure layer for AI compute. With H100/H200 sold out and Blackwell ramping, the company is entrenched in every major hyperscaler capex cycle. At -21% from highs on macro/tariff concerns rather than fundamental deterioration, this is an attractive long-term entry. Data center revenue growth remains robust and the competitive moat (CUDA ecosystem) is extraordinarily deep.

MSFT.thesis: Microsoft is the most diversified AI infrastructure play combining Azure cloud, OpenAI partnership, and enterprise software. Azure AI workloads are growing >50% YoY. The stock is -35% from its 52-week high, pricing in excessive pessimism. Copilot integration across Office 365 creates a durable recurring revenue stream. Strong FCF generation supports continued investment in AI infrastructure.

GOOGL.thesis: Alphabet operates one of the world's largest AI infrastructure networks via its custom TPU chips and global data centers. Google Cloud is growing rapidly with AI workloads. At -21% from highs and trading at reasonable multiples relative to growth, the market is undervaluing the optionality in DeepMind, Waymo, and AI-enhanced search monetization. The selloff appears macro-driven rather than fundamental.

AMZN.thesis: Amazon Web Services is the world's largest cloud provider and is deploying massive capex into AI infrastructure including custom Trainium/Inferentia chips. The combination of AWS AI services growth, advertising tailwinds, and logistics optimization via AI makes AMZN a diversified AI beneficiary. The stock has pulled back -23% from highs on macro concerns while fundamentals remain intact.

AVGO.thesis: Broadcom is the leading custom silicon (XPU/ASIC) partner for Google, Meta, and other hyperscalers building proprietary AI chips. This business is growing explosively and provides a high-margin alternative to NVDA for inference workloads. VMware integration is progressing ahead of schedule. At -27% from 52wk highs, the market undervalues the secular AI chip design opportunity.

ARM.thesis: ARM Holdings licenses the CPU architecture that underpins virtually all mobile and an increasing share of data center AI chips. The royalty model provides high operating leverage as ASP and complexity of chips increases with AI workloads. Recent relative strength (+11.5% 1M vs QQQ -7.7%) signals the market is recognizing ARM's central role in next-generation AI silicon. Custom server chips from Apple, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft all run on ARM.

MRVL.thesis: Marvell Technology is emerging as a top-tier custom silicon provider for AI data centers, competing directly for hyperscaler ASIC business alongside Broadcom. The electro-optics and interconnect portfolio is critical for high-bandwidth AI cluster networking. The +19.7% 1M return in a brutal tape signals fundamental outperformance. At -7.6% from 52wk highs, this is one of the strongest risk/reward setups in the AI infrastructure space.

META.thesis: Meta Platforms is one of the highest-quality internet businesses in the world, with 3+ billion daily active users across its family of apps and an advertising business that is structurally taking share from linear media. The company's aggressive AI investment — including its Llama models, AI recommendation systems, and Ray-Ban AI glasses — is already showing ROI through improved ad targeting and engagement metrics. At -34% from highs on tariff/macro concerns despite the business being fundamentally domestic US (minimal direct tariff exposure), the valuation is extremely attractive. Meta trades at roughly 22x forward earnings with 15-20% revenue growth guided — a significant discount to the S&P 500 multiple on an absolute basis. The $50B+ annual FCF funds massive buybacks (Meta repurchased 8% of shares outstanding in 2024) that compound per-share value even in sideways markets. Zuckerberg's clear AI vision and track record of pivoting successfully (Instagram acquisition, Reels pivot, now AI) give management high marks. This is one of the highest-conviction names in the universe at current prices.

COST.thesis: Costco Wholesale is one of the finest retail businesses ever built, with a membership-based model that creates extraordinary loyalty (renewal rates >90%), predictable recurring revenue, and a reputation for value that attracts members in good times and bad. The business is gaining market share in the current inflationary environment as consumers trade down to bulk purchasing. International expansion — particularly in Asia — provides a multi-year growth runway that is entirely self-funded by the business. The private label Kirkland brand continues to take shelf space and margin. Costco's -0.3% performance in a month when SPY fell 7.8% validates its defensive quality. While the valuation is not cheap at ~50x forward PE, Costco has consistently justified premium multiples through consistent high-single-digit revenue growth and member loyalty. This position provides crucial portfolio ballast when AI/tech faces macro headwinds.

TSM.thesis: Taiwan Semiconductor is the world's only manufacturer of leading-edge chips below 5nm, making it structurally irreplaceable for every AI semiconductor company in the portfolio and the global tech economy. • Moat: Technologically insurmountable manufacturing moat — 3nm/2nm process leadership is 2-3 years ahead of nearest competitor (Intel); switching costs are effectively infinite as no hyperscaler can abandon TSM's process without forfeiting AI chip competitiveness; scale advantages from $30B+ annual capex maintain the compounding lead. • Growth: Revenue growing 20% YoY, AI/HPC segment growing 50%+ and now represents >25% of revenue; CoWoS advanced packaging is sold out through 2025-26; TAM expanding as AI training/inference chips require increasingly advanced nodes; Arizona fab expansion (with $100B US commitment) reduces geopolitical risk premium over time. • Valuation: Trailing P/E 33x, fwd P/E 19x — historically cheap for TSM given growth rate; 45% net margins, 35% ROE, -12.2% from 52W high; sector avg fwd P/E for AI semis is 25-30x, so TSM is genuinely undervalued vs peers; geopolitical Taiwan risk discount is real but overstated given customer/US government dependency. • Catalyst: April 16 earnings report — Q1 revenue guidance was strong; AI/HPC demand commentary from CEO will be a key read-through for entire semiconductor complex; recent analyst upgrades (Nomura Taiwan fund +164%) signal institutional accumulation. • Entry: -12.2% from 52W high, consolidating around $341; entering ahead of earnings at historically reasonable valuation; swing trader long at same price confirms entry timing. • Sizing: 2.9% weight — starter position appropriate given earnings risk and cash constraints; will add on pullback or post-earnings confirmation.

PANW.thesis: Palo Alto Networks is the leading AI-native security platform uniquely positioned for the platformization era — consolidating enterprise security spend from 30+ point solutions into a single architecture with superior economics. • Moat: Platform switching costs are extraordinarily high once PANW's Cortex/Prisma suite is integrated across SOC, cloud, and network security; AI-powered Precision AI creates a data moat that improves with scale. • Growth: Revenue growing +15% YoY, transitioning to ARR/subscription model — Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) growing >20%; cybersecurity TAM expanding to $250B+ as AI increases both threat surface and security spend. • Valuation: Trailing P/E 90.7x on GAAP basis looks elevated, but fwd P/E 41.1x reflects the transition away from product revenue; FCF margins are ~25%+ and the platformization strategy is driving NDR >115%; CEO just bought $10M personally — rare conviction signal. • Catalyst: CEO's $10M personal purchase at ~$155-163 range signals strong insider conviction; cybersecurity sector in secular demand with AI expanding attack surface; earnings approaching where platformization metrics will be key. • Entry: Stock is at $163.21, -27% from 52W high (~$225), technically recovering from correction lows with volume support; insider buy at this level provides price support signal. • Sizing: ~0.8% portfolio weight — intentionally small starter position given cash constraints; max loss if stopped at 12% down is ~$98; sizing small because: (1) portfolio already has significant tech/AI concentration, (2) limited cash available after MRVL/CIEN trims cover this purchase

MU.thesis: Micron Technology is the pure-play beneficiary of the AI HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) supercycle — the only US manufacturer of leading-edge DRAM/NAND at the exact moment AI training and inference demand is creating structural memory shortages. • Moat: Micron is one of only three companies globally (DRAM: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix) capable of manufacturing HBM3/HBM3E at scale; US government strategic interest in domestic semiconductor manufacturing provides regulatory protection; technology leadership in 1-beta DRAM node is generating product differentiation. • Growth: Revenue growing 196% YoY — the fastest revenue acceleration in the portfolio by far; HBM revenue alone is expected to exceed $8B in FY2026; AI server DRAM content per server is growing 5-8x vs. traditional servers; SK Hynix cannot meet all demand, creating a long tail of Micron wins. • Valuation: Fwd P/E 4.7x is extraordinarily cheap — the market is treating MU as a commodity cyclical despite structural HBM demand that has multi-year visibility; trailing P/E 22x reflects the still-early stage of the cycle; at -1.2% from 52W high the market is beginning to re-rate. • Catalyst: SNDK joining Nasdaq-100 (storage momentum), swing trader already confirming with 8-share position, memory cycle clearly inflecting per Sandisk superbull thesis appearing in Yahoo Finance today — memory is the next AI infrastructure theme to run after semis and networking. • Entry: At $465.66, -1.2% from 52W high, breaking out to new highs — this is a momentum-confirmed breakout with fundamental support; entering as the memory supercycle thesis becomes mainstream. • Sizing: 10 shares at ~4.2% weight is a conviction position but not maximum — leaving room to add on earnings confirmation; memory cycle timing is less certain than the ASIC/networking thesis so sizing below AVGO/MRVL/NVDA is appropriate.

AMD.thesis: AMD is the #2 data center GPU platform with a proven and accelerating customer adoption curve, validated by tonight's earnings beat with strong AI data center commentary. • Moat: AMD's RDNA/CDNA GPU architecture combined with ROCm software stack creates meaningful switching costs for HPC/AI workloads; x86 CPU dominance in server creates halo effect for GPU cross-selling; open ecosystem approach differentiates from NVDA's closed CUDA lock-in, appealing to hyperscalers seeking supply diversification • Growth: 34% revenue growth trajectory driven by data center GPU ramp; MI300/MI350 GPU family gaining hyperscaler wins; AMD's data center segment growing >80% YoY per recent reports; TAM expanding as inference workloads require alternative GPU supply chains • Valuation: 31.7x fwd P/E for 34% growth yields PEG <1x — genuinely cheap relative to AI semiconductor peers; NVDA at 17.5x fwd P/E benefits from earnings acceleration at much higher absolute earnings base; AMD is earlier in the earnings ramp with more upside to estimates • Catalyst: Q1 2026 earnings beat tonight with strong data center GPU guidance confirmed per Barrons — 'AMD Stock Jumps on Strong Earnings and Growing Confidence About AI'; this is the exact post-print confirmation entry I have been planning for since my prior memory notes • Entry: Post-earnings entry at ~$355 is ideal — AMD at -2.1% from 52W high with momentum intact; entering after print eliminates binary earnings risk; swing trader already holds 9 shares at +61.3% confirming institutional momentum • Sizing: ~2.6% portfolio weight is a starter position limited by cash; max position would be 10-12% of portfolio (~$12-15K) representing 34-42 shares — will add on any pullback as cash replenishes

ALAB.thesis: Astera Labs is the dominant provider of CXL and PCIe connectivity silicon enabling AI clusters to scale beyond single-node GPU boundaries — an essential infrastructure layer for every hyperscaler building 100K+ GPU clusters. • Moat: ALAB holds leading market share in CXL retimers and smart cable modules with 2+ year product lead over competitors; deep co-development relationships with hyperscalers create powerful switching costs; ARIES/TAURUS/LEO product families address the full connectivity stack creating platform stickiness • Growth: 92% revenue growth rate, TAM expanding from ~$2B today to $15B+ by 2028 as AI cluster sizes scale; every GPU node added requires ALAB connectivity silicon; Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta all confirmed as customers; CXL memory pooling is the next major catalyst as inference workloads demand cost-efficient memory • Valuation: 49.6x fwd P/E for 92% growth = PEG of ~0.54x — genuinely undervalued relative to growth trajectory; 143.6x trailing P/E reflects recent profitability inflection; sector average for high-growth semis is 80-120x trailing — ALAB is cheap on a forward basis • Catalyst: Just delivered back-to-back beat-and-raise quarters with Q1 2026 confirmed by Zacks; hyperscaler AI capex cycle at record levels with $700B+ committed for 2026; CXL adoption moving from early deployment to mainstream in 2026-2027 • Entry: $213.91 is -18.6% from 52W high, having pulled back from the post-earnings pop; entering after confirmation of the fundamental trajectory rather than ahead of uncertainty; swing trader holding 18 shares confirms short-term momentum is constructive • Sizing: 1.85% starter weight — appropriate for a name with high growth visibility but still elevated multiple; not larger because cash is limited and the position can be built over time as CXL adoption data points accumulate

ANET.thesis:
Arista Networks is the dominant provider of 400G/800G data center networking switches for hyperscaler AI clusters — an essential infrastructure layer for every large-scale GPU deployment.
• Moat: Near-monopoly in cloud networking with 35%+ market share at the high end; EOS operating system creates extraordinary switching costs (customers never want to retrain network engineers on a new OS); deep co-development relationships with Microsoft, Meta, and Google for custom AI networking architectures
• Growth: 35% revenue growth with 38% operating margins — best margin profile in enterprise networking; TAM expanding as AI clusters grow from 10K to 100K+ GPUs requiring proportionally more spine/leaf networking; hyperscaler capex cycle just confirmed at record levels (MSFT Azure beat, AWS beat, Google Cloud +28%)
• Valuation: 41.4x fwd P/E for 35% growth with 38% margins — PEG of ~1.2x is reasonable for a best-in-class compounder; historically traded at 45-60x fwd P/E; current valuation is at the low end of historical range
• Catalyst: Q2 earnings tonight (Aug 4) — hyperscaler AI capex confirmation from MSFT and AMZN earnings last week is the most constructive possible read-through; if Azure AI workloads are accelerating, Arista's data center switches are in every one of those deployments
• Entry: -2.6% from 52W high after +8.3% 1W recovery; technically strong with momentum improving post-hyperscaler earnings beats; buying at fair value into a confirmed AI capex acceleration cycle
• Sizing: 2.8% starter position; max loss if thesis breaks and stock falls 20% = ~$740; not larger because we are buying into earnings; will add on strength post-earnings confirmation or on any pullback that keeps thesis intact

COHR.thesis:
Coherent is the leading supplier of optical components and transceivers for AI data center interconnects, with the AI buildout driving unprecedented demand for 400G/800G/1.6T optical networking components used in hyperscaler GPU clusters.
• Moat: Leading market share in indium phosphide laser epitaxy and vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) used in AI optical interconnects; deep customer relationships with hyperscalers creating substantial switching costs; vertical integration from wafer to module provides cost advantages and supply reliability that competitors cannot match
• Growth: 20% revenue growth at 42.5x fwd P/E; Lumentum's +15% earnings blowout directly validates the AI optical demand cycle; AI data center interconnect market growing 40%+ annually as GPU cluster density increases; CoreWeave and Supermicro beats confirm AI infrastructure investment cycle intact; FN reports Aug 17 as additional catalyst
• Valuation: 42.5x fwd P/E is not cheap for 20% growth but fair given: (1) post-earnings de-risking, (2) AI optical demand inflection creating potential for growth acceleration above 20%, (3) -19.2% from 52W high creates margin of safety vs recent ATH
• Catalyst: Post-earnings clarity — the binary earnings risk has cleared with solid results; Lumentum +15% blowout is the most bullish possible read-through; FN earnings Aug 17 is the next AI optical data point
• Entry: $355 is +8.3% 1W post-earnings — not chasing; the stock is still -19.2% from 52W high (~$440); entry after earnings removes key risk; volume ratio 1.66 shows elevated institutional interest
• Sizing: 2.1% weight — small starter limited by cash constraint; max loss if stop hit (15%) = ~$426; would prefer larger position but cash discipline requires this size; conviction warrants initiating even at starter size
